paragraphs: LVMH is a French luxury company. It owns famous brands such as Louis Vuitton, Dior and Sephora. Its brands sell clothes, bags, watches, perfume and wine. It sells expensive goods to wealthy shoppers around the world. On October 12, the company shared its sales results for the first nine months of 2026.

From January to September, LVMH had revenue of 57.1 billion euros. On an organic basis, its revenue grew 2%. Organic growth does not count changes in currency exchange rates. It also does not count businesses that the company bought or sold. In other words, it compares the same businesses in the same money. For example, a strong euro can make sales in other countries look smaller than they really are.

The third quarter, from July to September, was weaker. Organic growth was only 1%, a slight rise. According to LVMH, the main reason was China, where demand was less strong. Nevertheless, the United States, Europe and Japan saw good growth.

Fashion and leather goods is the company's largest division. It had revenue of 26.4 billion euros in the nine months. LVMH relies on this division more than on any other part of its business. But here the results showed a decrease. Organic revenue fell 2% in the nine months. In the third quarter alone, the decrease was 5%. The division did well in the United States. However, it was hurt by weaker demand in China. When wealthy shoppers in China spend less, LVMH quickly feels it.

The fashion brands still had news to share. Louis Vuitton held a celebration because its Monogram is now 130 years old. The Monogram is the pattern on many of its iconic bags. The celebration included a new version of the pattern. In September, Dior opened a new store on Via Monte Napoleone in Milan. Furthermore, on September 1, LVMH sold the brand Marc Jacobs to WHP Global.

Other parts of the group did better. Watches & Jewelry grew 8% in the nine months and 6% in the third quarter. Selective Retailing, the segment that includes Sephora, grew 6% in the nine months. In the third quarter, its growth was even stronger, at 8%. Sephora sells beauty products from many different brands. The report also highlights new Sephora stores in two countries, Belgium and Croatia. Sales of perfume and beauty products showed stability. Their organic revenue did not change in the nine months.

Overall, the results demonstrate a year of moderate growth for LVMH. Some segments rely on new products and new stores to keep growing. Others need shoppers in China to return. Stability in some parts of the business helps, but moderate growth is not what investors hope for. The results also demonstrate how much the iconic fashion brands matter. The company says it wants to make its position as the world's leader in luxury goods even stronger in 2026.
